newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to decide on maize export support in March.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to decide on maize export support in March.

text.p: Hungary will decide in March whether it will subsidise maize exports in an effort to reduce stocks, an Agriculture Ministry official said on Thursday.
"Based on how exports will be going until then, we will decide whether export subsidies are necessary," said Balazs Tarjan, head of the ministry's agricultural regime office.
Hungarian grain dealers have said that Hungary's excess maize, estimated at between 500,000 and one million tonnes, has difficulties finding export markets.
Most European countries have enough maize to last until the next harvest and exports outside Europe are uneconomical, they said.
There are currently no export subsidies in Hungary, and export permits cost 2,000 forints a tonne which is refundable if the maize is exported, Tarjan said.
The ministry recently gave permits for the export of 200,000 tonnes of maize, which Tarjan expected would actually be exported, albeit in small deals.
